verdict.rationale: Trigger.dev documents a local dev command that runs a server on the developer's machine to execute tasks. Self-hosting via `docker compose up` gives a local instance, and users independently praise Dev mode and easy local testing. The CI-testing half of the story is not evidenced: the GitHub Actions doc covers deploying tasks, not running them in CI. missing for 10: documented CI test execution of workflows (e.g., running tasks against a dev/test environment in a CI pipeline), detailed docs on dev-environment isolation and testing utilities.

support.subject: As a developer, I can run workflows locally or against a dev instance for development and CI testing

citations.quote: This runs a server on your machine that can execute Trigger.dev tasks
Testing and local development is easy as can be. No complex configurations.
Also want to call out the Dev mode: it's an absolute gem, makes testing and iterating so much smoother than anything else I've tried.
No more startup scripts, just `docker compose up`.
